title: A Comprehensive Calibration Standard for CryoEM Workflow Validation
content: Cryogenic electron microscopy (cryoEM) has enabled structural biology techniques to characterize molecular and cellular processes. The National Center for CryoEM Access and Training (NCCAT) is an NIH-sponsored cryoEM service center housed at the New York Structural Biology Center (NYSBC) that offers nationwide access to cryoEM instrumentation, screening, and training at no cost at the point of access [1,2]. An important part of NCCAT's mission is to broaden access to high-resolution cryoEM technologies for biomedical researchers and cultivating a skilled workforce through the development and implementation of cryoEM training material. However, the complex and varied nature of cryoEM instrumentation necessitates precise benchmarking to ensure optimal performance and data quality. We introduce the concept of a cryoEM Ladder, a novel calibration standard designed to extend beyond resolution benchmarking and address the several necessary metrics required to be met during cryoEM workflow validation [3]. Each cryoEM setup is unique, influenced by its specific configuration and local environment factors.
